_meta.note: Canonical research data. Edit these files (or regenerate), then run pipeline/validate.py and pipeline/export.py.

sources.title: Of Human Bondage (Project Gutenberg eBook #351)
sources.license_reuse: Public domain in the USA (Project Gutenberg licence). Maugham d. 1965: still in copyright in life+70 jurisdictions (UK/EU) until end of 2035.
sources.contains: Full text, 122 chapters, plain text.
sources.usefulness: high — full-text extraction with chapter locators
sources.automatable: yes — plain text, stable URL, chapter headings are bare roman numerals

sources.title: L'Éducation sentimentale, v. 1 (Œuvres complètes de Gustave Flaubert, tome 3; Project Gutenberg eBook #49773)
sources.contains: French text, Part I and Part II ch. I–III.
sources.usefulness: high — original-language anchors

sources.title: L'Éducation sentimentale, v. 2 (Œuvres complètes de Gustave Flaubert, tome 4; Project Gutenberg eBook #52893)
sources.contains: French text, Part II ch. IV–VI and Part III.
sources.usefulness: high — original-language anchors

sources.title: Sentimental Education; Or, The History of a Young Man, Volume 1 (Project Gutenberg eBook #34828)
sources.institution_or_author: Gustave Flaubert (anonymous English translation); Project Gutenberg
sources.contains: English translation, chapters I–X (continuous numbering, not Flaubert's three parts).
sources.usefulness: medium — English display anchors; chapter numbering differs from the French, so a concordance is needed
sources.notes: Downloaded and inspected; not yet used for anchors. Volume 2 is eBook #27537.

sources.title: The Razor's Edge (Faded Page eBook #20171032)
sources.institution_or_author: W. Somerset Maugham; Distributed Proofreaders Canada
sources.license_reuse: Public domain in Canada only. The file states: "If the book is under copyright in your country, do not download or redistribute this file." In copyright in the USA (published 1944) and in life+70 jurisdictions until end of 2035. Text was consulted to locate mentions and is NOT stored in this workspace; only short anchors are recorded.
sources.contains: Full text, seven chapters with numbered sections.
sources.usefulness: high for locating mentions; RESTRICTED for reuse
sources.notes: Every Razor's Edge anchor should be re-checked against a licensed edition before publication, and page numbers added from that edition.

sources.title: Tropic of Cancer — publisher excerpt (opening section)
sources.institution_or_author: Henry Miller; Grove Atlantic / Grove Press
sources.license_reuse: In copyright (Miller d. 1980; © Grove Press). Short quotation only. Excerpt is not stored in this workspace.
sources.contains: Authorised excerpt of the opening section (about 40,000 characters), no pagination.
sources.usefulness: high for the opening section only; the rest of the novel is not covered

sources.title: The Magician, with "A Fragment of Autobiography" (Project Gutenberg eBook #14257)
sources.license_reuse: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg.
sources.contains: Maugham's own preface describing his 1905 flat near the Lion de Belfort and the restaurant Le Chat Blanc, rue d'Odessa.
sources.usefulness: high — first-person evidence for biographical places behind both Maugham novels

sources.title: Wikidata
sources.contains: Work identifiers (QID, VIAF, BnF, Open Library, Gutenberg ID), author identifiers, narrative location (P840), derivative works, place entities with coordinates (P625), addresses, dissolution dates.
sources.usefulness: high — canonical IDs and coordinates for 99 of the places here; weak for work-to-place links (P840 only gives "Paris")
sources.automatable: yes — SPARQL endpoint and wbsearchentities API
sources.notes: Crowd-sourced: coordinates and unsourced statements are treated as strongly_supported at best, never verified. Street coordinates are a single representative point.

sources.title: Dénominations caduques des voies
sources.contains: 9,103 obsolete Paris street names with the decree that renamed them and the current name.
sources.usefulness: high — resolves historic street names in 19th-century texts to current streets

sources.title: Dénominations des emprises des voies actuelles
sources.contains: 6,625 current Paris streets with history notes ("historique"), endpoints, arrondissement and quartier.
sources.usefulness: medium — authoritative current names and street histories; not yet joined to PLACE records
sources.notes: Schema inspected; no records ingested yet.

sources.title: Plaques commémoratives
sources.contains: 2,619 commemorative plaques with transcription, address and coordinates.
sources.usefulness: medium — verified biographical addresses with coordinates (found Flaubert, 42 boulevard du Temple; nothing for Maugham, Rhys or Henry Miller)

sources.title: Lieux de tournage à Paris
sources.contains: 15,852 filming permits (title, director, year, address, coordinates) for shoots from 2016 onward.
sources.usefulness: none for these five works (no adaptation shot in the period); high for recent films
sources.notes: Queried by title for all five works and their adaptations: zero relevant records.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap via Nominatim
sources.contains: Geocoding of specific street addresses to OSM nodes.
sources.usefulness: medium — house-number coordinates where Wikidata has only the street
sources.automatable: yes — within the 1 request/second usage policy; bulk work needs a self-hosted instance or the BAN (Base Adresse Nationale)
sources.notes: Gives the present-day position of a house number. House numbering can change; a 19th-century number is not guaranteed to be the same building.

sources.title: data.bnf.fr / BnF catalogue général
sources.contains: Work and author authority records (ARK identifiers), editions; SPARQL endpoint.
sources.usefulness: medium — authority IDs and edition metadata; no place-level data
sources.notes: ARK numbers taken from Wikidata P268, not yet confirmed on data.bnf.fr itself.

sources.title: Blue plaque: RHYS, Jean (1890–1979), Paultons House
sources.contains: Plaque record and narrative: Rhys lived in Flat 22, Paultons House, 1936–1938 and wrote Good Morning, Midnight there.
sources.usefulness: high — institutional statement of composition place
sources.automatable: partial — one HTML page per plaque; no bulk API found

sources.title: Parcours parisien : à la recherche des personnages littéraires
sources.institution_or_author: Bibliothèques de la Ville de Paris
sources.contains: List of about twenty plaques for fictional characters at Paris addresses, including Frédéric Moreau (L'Éducation sentimentale) at 13, rue de Choiseul.
sources.usefulness: medium — institutional, small, but exactly the work-to-address link Dérive needs; companion book "À Paris, sur les pas des personnages de romans" (Autrement) has twenty maps
sources.automatable: partial — HTML list only; the page mentions an interactive map but no open-data link was found

sources.title: Reading and Georeferencing Rhys (Z-Axis Research Initiative)
sources.institution_or_author: Adèle Barclay; Maker Lab in the Humanities, University of Victoria (PI Jentery Sayers); Modernist Versions Project
sources.contains: Method note: the whole novel was georeferenced and word counts per location computed to drive 3D "z-axis" maps of Paris. Names Boulevard du Montparnasse and the Quartier Latin as locations of Sasha's movements.
sources.usefulness: low as data (the georeferenced table was not published); medium as corroboration and method precedent

sources.title: uvicmakerlab/zaxis — Materials for the Z-Axis Research Initiative
sources.institution_or_author: Maker Lab in the Humanities, University of Victoria
sources.contains: Mudbox meshes (1932 Paris; Rhys's Quartet, chapter 1) and a Ulysses data model spreadsheet.
sources.usefulness: none for the five works — no Good Morning, Midnight data in the repository
sources.automatable: yes for what is there (GitHub API)
sources.notes: Checked the full file tree: Good Morning, Midnight georeferences are not included.

sources.title: "Nobody Else Knows Me, but the Street Knows Me" — Jean Rhys's Urban Flaneuses: Mapping "Good Morning, Midnight"
sources.institution_or_author: Emily Duffy; Ursinus College (independent study project)
sources.contains: Spatial reading of the novel with a supplementary file "Rhys Map Index.docx" indexing mapped places.
sources.usefulness: potentially high — the only place index for this novel found; NOT retrieved
sources.automatable: no — repository is behind a bot challenge; needs a manual download
sources.notes: Metadata and abstract read; PDF and index returned HTTP 403 to automated requests. Top manual-retrieval priority for Good Morning, Midnight.

sources.title: Jean Rhys's Hotels of Flux and Comfort (HOTEMS: Hotels and the Modern Subject, 1890–1940)
sources.institution_or_author: Laura Oulanne; HOTEMS project, National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
sources.contains: Essay quoting the novel's hotel passages with page references; the project has a "Hotel Atlas" section.
sources.usefulness: medium — scholarly quotation of the "hotel without a name" passage; no addresses

sources.title: Gendered Urban Spaces and Strangeness in Jean Rhys' Good Morning, Midnight (1939)
sources.institution_or_author: Carla Martínez del Barrio; Odisea 22 (2021), 137–149. DOI 10.25115/odisea.v0i22.5485
sources.contains: Spatial/gender reading; names categories of space (streets, cafés, cinema, parks, shops) but almost no specific toponyms.
sources.usefulness: low for place data
sources.notes: Full text read; points to Britzolakis 2007, "This Way to the Exhibition" (Textual Practice 21.3), not retrieved.

sources.title: William Somerset Maugham (1874–1965) — Kent Maps Online
sources.contains: States that Whitstable and Canterbury are disguised as Blackstable and Tercanbury in Maugham's fiction; King's School, Canterbury.
sources.usefulness: medium — citable identification of the two fictional Kent towns; the wider project maps Kent writers
sources.automatable: partial — static site; underlying map data not located

sources.title: Henry MILLER à Paris, Clichy et ailleurs
sources.license_reuse: Creative Commons (variant not specified on the page)
sources.contains: Chronological list of Miller's addresses in Paris, Clichy and Dijon with dates; cites Temple, Perlès and Murat.
sources.usefulness: medium-high — address-level biography; the site covers hundreds of French-language writers
sources.automatable: partial — consistent one-page-per-author layout, no API
sources.notes: Page is Latin-1 encoded; quotations were re-accented by hand. Its dating of the Dijon post (winter 1932–1933) sits awkwardly with its own Clichy dates: see conflict queue.

sources.title: 18 Villa Seurat — The Paris Atlas
sources.contains: Claim-level entry for the address, citing Brassaï, biographies and OpenStreetMap.
sources.usefulness: medium — structured, sourced and uncertainty-aware; but a commercial site whose prose and illustrations may be machine-assisted, so follow its citations rather than cite it alone
sources.automatable: partial — pages carry schema.org JSON-LD; robots.txt disallows /api/
sources.notes: Already listed in the Dérive Source Registry as "Paris Atlas". No pages exist there for Maugham or Rhys (HTTP 404).

sources.title: Tropic of Cancer — The Paris Atlas
sources.contains: Book entry with summary, linked locations and a reference list (Brassaï 1995; Pearson 2007; two 1991 biographies; Grove excerpt).
sources.usefulness: medium — good pointer list; led to the authorised Grove excerpt

sources.title: Tropic of Cancer (novel) — English Wikipedia
sources.contains: Identifies the fictional Villa Borghese as 18 Villa Seurat (citing D'Abate 2018); composition context citing Brassaï 1995, pp. 105–107; 1970 film adaptation.
sources.usefulness: medium — discovery and citation trail

sources.title: Dérive Spatial Narrative Atlas, EN v3 (existing product workbook)
sources.contains: 31 work–place rows for Before Sunset, The Sun Also Rises and A Moveable Feast; ontology and source registry sheets.
sources.usefulness: high — defines the export schema and the places to deduplicate against
sources.notes: Read only. Nothing in web/ was modified.

sources.title: Centre Flaubert — L'Éducation sentimentale (texte de 1869; exemplaire Charpentier corrigé)
sources.institution_or_author: Centre Flaubert, Université de Rouen Normandie
sources.contains: Scholarly online text of the 1869 edition and a page-turner of the Charpentier copy corrected by Flaubert; extensive Flaubert resources.
sources.usefulness: high potential — the reference scholarly site; no place index or map for this novel was found in this pass
sources.notes: Specific URLs (oeuvres/ES_1869.php; jet/public/feuilletoir) were seen in a search summary and not opened. Check for a topographic index before doing more manual work on this novel.

sources.title: L'Éducation sentimentale — scénarios, brouillons et notes (NAF 17599–17611); manuscrit autographe définitif (BHVP, Rés. Ms 98)
sources.institution_or_author: Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département des Manuscrits; Bibliothèque historique de la Ville de Paris
sources.license_reuse: Gallica: non-commercial reuse free; commercial reuse licensed
sources.contains: Thirteen volumes of drafts and scenarios; definitive autograph manuscript at the BHVP.
sources.usefulness: medium — for composition and inspiration claims, not for place extraction
sources.notes: Shelfmarks reported in a search summary of a HAL notice (halshs-02117775); not independently confirmed.

sources.title: Internet Archive — lending-library scans of Tropic of Cancer, Good Morning, Midnight and The Razor's Edge
sources.contains: Page-image scans with OCR (e.g. goodmorningmidni0000rhys, Harper & Row 1970; tropicofcancer00mill, Grove 1961).
sources.usefulness: would be high — full text with page numbers
sources.automatable: no — full text and search-inside are access-controlled (HTTP 401/403)
sources.notes: Access controls were respected. A person with a library login or a print copy can verify anchors and page numbers.

sources.title: Around Paris With Good Morning, Midnight — Part 1
sources.contains: Reader's walk-through of the novel's Paris places.
sources.usefulness: low — candidate generation only

sources.title: Search-engine summary of unidentified secondary pages on Good Morning, Midnight
sources.contains: Reported a bar "the Pig and Lily" in "one of those streets at the back of the Montparnasse station".
sources.usefulness: very low — unattributed; kept only so the candidate is not lost
sources.notes: Not evidence. Used for one unresolved candidate.

sources.title: VIAF — Virtual International Authority File
sources.contains: Clustered authority identifiers for authors and works.
sources.usefulness: medium — identity reconciliation across national libraries
